newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Quantum surges on gold find talk.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Quantum surges on gold find talk.

text.p: Quantum Resources Ltd shares surged nearly nine percent on market talk that Joseph Gutnick's Johnson's Well Mining NL may have made a gold discovery in Western Australia, brokers said.
Quantum holds a 47.51 percent stake in Johnson's Well.
At 12.35 p.m. (0235 GMT), Quantum shares were 11 cents, or 8.9 percent, stronger at A$1.35. The stock has risen about 47 percent since August 8 when it closed at 92 cents.
"The rumour is that Johnson's Well may have made some sort of mineral discovery in Western Australia which they are not in a position to announce yet," a Brisbane-based broker said.
Johnson's Well officials were unavailable for comment. Its stock was untraded on Tuesday, after last trading at A$3.00 on Friday, and its buy-sell quotes were a wide A$3.00/A$3.50.
The broker said investors tended to trade Johnson's Well through Quantum because stock in the Gutnick company was so tightly held.

A Sydney-based gold analyst said although he had not heard the rumour, it was a possible explanation for the share price rise. "I wouldn't be surprised if Johnson's Well have found something, given the money they've been throwing at exploration," he said.
The Australian Stock Exchange on Monday queried Quantum about its climbing share price with the company replying that it had no explanation.
However, it did say it expected an operating loss before abnormals and tax of A$1.97 million for the 1995/96 year.
"It's normal for them to be having a loss because they are not producing, just exploring, so the statement to the stock exchange is probably irrelevant," the Brisbane broker said.
At 1.00 p.m. (0300 GMT), about 1.96 million Quantum shares had changed hands. Brokers said Epic Securities Ltd was the main buyer. -- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373 1800
